si_3_author_journal_year.answer: Itälinna et al., PLoS Computational Biology, 2023

si_4_title.answer: Using normative modeling and machine learning for detecting mild traumatic brain injury from magnetoencephalography data

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used a simple Z-score normative modeling approach where mean (μ) and standard deviation (σ) were calculated across subjects from the normative dataset. The deviation scores (Z-scores) were calculated as Z = (X - μ) / σ for each frequency and cortical location. This is a parametric approach based on ordinary mean and standard deviation calculations. For classification, an SVM classifier was used, but the normative modeling itself relies on simple summary statistics.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: In this study, a relatively simple and straightforward calculation of Z-scores was adapted, as robust statistical inference was not of concern: the normative modeling provided features for supervised machine learning rather than being directly used for discriminating patients from controls.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Italinna2023.pdf.md: Discussion / Normative modeling: Advantages and considerations

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Source-level power spectral densities (PSDs) were computed from resting-state MEG recordings at cortical locations. The PSDs were binned into six canonical frequency bands: delta (1-4 Hz), theta (4-8 Hz), alpha (8-13 Hz), low beta (13-17 Hz), high beta (17-30 Hz), and gamma (30-40 Hz). The spatial dimension was parcellated into 448 cortical regions.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: An automated source-modeling pipeline was applied on the measurements to compute power spectral densities (PSDs) at each cortical location using the MNE-Python software.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age was used as the basis for constructing age-matched normative models. The normative data was stratified by age decades (18-27, 28-37, 38-47, 48-57, 58-67 years) to create age-matched subsets. However, in the primary analysis using the full normative dataset, age was not explicitly modeled as a covariate in a regression sense; rather, the entire healthy population was used to compute population-level statistics.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: To test the effect of using normative data from a specific age group, the model was trained and evaluated on an age-matched subset of the normative data, i.e., only the power spectra belonging to the same age decade as the subject were used. The age groups were defined according to the normative dataset as 18-27, 28-37, 38-47, 48-57 and 58-67 years.
